name: a_component_inside_a_sub_assembly_is_refused
why: Z-C21.5, findings L11-3 and L11-5. The C1..Cn of the assembly state list EVERY level (GetComponents(false), on purpose: a sub-assembly shown as one block with nothing inside would hide thirty parts), while the two SOLIDWORKS calls behind fissa_componente and sostituisci_componente work on the top level only: IsFixed «only applies to the top level of components» (IComponent2~IsFixed.html) and ReplaceComponents2 wants «a top-level component. It cannot be a component of a sub-assembly» (IAssemblyDoc~ReplaceComponents2.html). Up to library 0.145.0 neither operation looked, and sostituisci_componente counted the swap as done when ANY component of the assembly used the new file. No case could show it, because the bench could not build a sub-assembly: a component with a list of `componenti` of its own is now one.
defect_caught: A nested component fixed, freed or replaced from the root as if it were a top-level one; «it was already fixed/free: nothing to change» read from an IsFixed that does not apply; a replacement that did not happen reported as made because another component (here «spare», mounted at the top level) already used the new file; the state calling a nested component fixed or free, or counting it among the loose ones, when from the root its state is not known.
_if_it_stays_green_on_the_old_library: It does not: on 0.145.0 step 1 either answers «already fixed» or calls FixComponent on the nested pin, never the top-level refusal the case asks for; step 2 calls ReplaceComponents2 on the nested pin and, whatever that does, finds «spare» on the new file and reports the swap as made. Step 3 asks for «top_level» and «nested_components», which the old state does not write.
_the_numbers: Names decide the uids (sorted, Name2 of a nested component is the whole path «group-1/pin-1»): C1 base, C2 the sub-assembly «group», C3 the pin inside it, C4 the plate inside it, C5 spare. The base went in first, so SOLIDWORKS fixed it; the sub-assembly and spare are floating; the pin went in first INSIDE the sub-assembly. Top-level: base, group, spare (3); nested: pin, plate (2).

expect.why: the sub-assembly went in second: floating. Nothing of step 1 fixed it
the sub-assembly itself is a top-level component: fixing it is allowed, and read back with IsFixed
the pin is inside «group»: its name is «group-1/pin-1», not one of GetComponents(true)
IsFixed does not apply to a nested component: «not known from here», not true (the pin is the first component of its sub-assembly) and not false
the base (fixed by SOLIDWORKS) and the sub-assembly (fixed by this step); the nested ones are not counted
only spare: a nested component moves with its sub-assembly and is not judged on its own, or the plate would be called loose in every rigid sub-assembly
a top-level component is replaced: the base takes the file of spare, which was already mounted, and the check now asks about the base itself, not about any component on that file
there were no mates to lose
